tts_summary:
Here is your midday market update for Tuesday, September 22nd.

The broad market is treading water. The S&P 500 is essentially flat, the Nasdaq is up about 38 basis points, the Russell 2000 is up 30 basis points, and the Dow is lagging, down 43 basis points. Treasuries are flat across the curve. Brent crude is hovering near one hundred dollars a barrel, off modestly, as diplomatic signals out of the United Nations suggest some hope for de-escalation with Iran. Iran has reportedly offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days if the US takes initial steps to ease military pressure. Saudi Arabia is also showing signs of bringing its East-West Pipeline back online after Houthi disruptions forced crude back through Hormuz. These developments are keeping energy in check and providing a mild tailwind for risk sentiment — but markets are not making a big move either way yet.

The bigger near-term catalyst investors are focused on is the AI event calendar. Zuckerberg's Meta Connect keynote is Wednesday night, OpenAI's developer day is September 29th, and Micron reports earnings on September 30th. That is a packed ten days for the AI trade, and it explains why semiconductor and AI-linked names are leading today — names like Micron, ARM, Alphabet, Meta, Marvell, and Oracle are all outperforming.

On the company side, Meta is in focus after its Muse personal AI agent is seeing a surge in downloads. Shopify announced it will allow Muse to complete purchases on its platform — a meaningful agentic commerce win for both companies, and a contrast to Amazon which has blocked Muse entirely. OpenAI is also reportedly working on a competing product.

On earnings, AutoZone beat on fiscal fourth quarter earnings per share — fifty-six dollars and five cents versus the fifty-four dollars expected — but the quality was low. The beat was almost entirely driven by tariff refunds and a non-cash accounting benefit, while domestic comps missed badly at plus 1.6 versus the plus 3.1 the Street expected. Management's positive linearity comments are helping the stock hold up. MillerKnoll was a cleaner beat — fifty-three cents versus thirty-six cents expected, and even stripping out the tariff refund tailwind, they still beat. THOR Industries missed, with gross margins down 230 basis points year-over-year, and management flagged a tough macro environment. Viking Therapeutics reported impressive trial data for its GLP-1 obesity drug, showing 22 percent weight loss. Cognex is acquiring a depth-sensing camera company for roughly 500 million dollars to build out its Physical AI capabilities.

On the downside, lab testing names Quest Diagnostics and Lab Corp are getting hit after CMS released Medicare lab payment rates that came in worse than expected. The financial complex broadly — banks, brokers, insurers, asset managers, and managed care — is underperforming.

Directionally, the tape is neutral with a cautiously constructive tilt toward the AI theme. The next ten days of catalysts will be decisive for whether the tech leadership trade has legs into year-end. Watch the Meta keynote Wednesday night as the first major signal.
